wrapup.desc: When this agent ends due to timeout or running out of steps, the system injects this "wrap-up prompt" and runs one final round. It first re-records anything identified but not yet saved, then outputs a one-sentence summary (to avoid leaving things unfinished). Leave blank to use the built-in default.

taskTimeout.desc: Task timeout wrap-up (a separate set from the per-run wrap-up above): injected when the entire task reaches its timeout limit and is about to end. Its intent is often the opposite of per-run. For example, in per-run a planner says "don't stop, keep planning," but on task timeout it says "stop on time and make a final judgment." Leave blank to use the built-in default.

triggers.desc: Triggers run this custom agent automatically. Each time one fires, it creates and runs a new session (visible on the "Conversations" page). You can select multiple trigger conditions, and the system automatically appends "the reason it fired this time + the related task/vulnerability/goal" after the base message you wrote.
triggers.policyLabel: Post-trigger handling policy (determines how triggers are queued, merged, and run)
triggers.policyParallel: Parallel: each trigger immediately opens its own session and runs concurrently, with no merging. Triggers beyond the max concurrent runs wait in the queue for a free slot.
triggers.policyByTask: Serial, merge by task: the same agent runs only one at a time, and event triggers for the same task are merged into one session in the queue.
triggers.policyAll: Serial, merge all: the same agent runs only one at a time, and when the queue is dequeued, all currently waiting triggers are merged into one session.
triggers.policyNone: Serial, no merging: the same agent runs only one at a time, and each trigger opens its own session.

trafficCapture.title: Traffic Capture
trafficCapture.desc:
When on, all agents' HTTP traffic passes through the recording proxy and is fully saved, and the traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy settings are injected into the agents (the prompt includes a proxy description).

When off (default), no traffic is recorded. Agents do not receive the proxy settings or traffic tools, and the prompt does not include any proxy-related content. Toggling regenerates the agents immediately to apply the change.
trafficCapture.on: On · Recording traffic and injecting the proxy
trafficCapture.off: Off · No recording or proxy injection

agentBinding.title: Automatic Agent Traffic Binding
agentBinding.desc:
Off by default. When on, the report agent that runs when a finding is recorded cross-checks existing HTTP requests/responses, links the relevant traffic, and then writes the report. Inspecting packets and making extra tool calls increases token usage.

It can still report normally when the traffic is TCP, no packets were captured, or there is no matching traffic. This switch does not affect traffic capture, manual linking, or viewing saved evidence. It applies starting from the next round of agents, and turning it off immediately rejects new automatic links.

globalProxy.title: Global Proxy
globalProxy.desc:
All agents' destination traffic goes out through this proxy (hides the source IP / uses a relay server). It supports http / https / socks5 and can include user:pass authentication. Leave empty for a direct connection.

When Traffic Capture is on, this proxy becomes the upstream of the recording proxy (traffic is still fully saved and then goes out through this proxy again). When capture is off, it is injected directly into the agents' bash / WebFetch output. It is independent of the web search proxy and the LLM proxy.

Note: With capture off, socks5 depends on whether each command-line tool supports ALL_PROXY (curl does, but some tools may ignore it). If you mainly use socks5, it's better to turn on Traffic Capture. On that path the MITM makes the connection directly, so it applies reliably even if a tool doesn't notice.
globalProxy.placeholder: socks5://user:pass@host:1080 or http://host:port (empty for direct connection)
globalProxy.configured: Configured · All destination traffic goes out through this proxy
globalProxy.notConfigured: Not configured · Destination traffic goes out via direct connection

constraints.title: Behavior Constraint Injection
constraints.desc:
When on, each task's behavior constraints (the allow/deny items managed under “Behavior Constraints” in the task overview) are appended to that agent's system prompt to limit the exploration scope (e.g., “Test the current port only”, “No brute forcing”).

You can control injection separately for the planner and the worker; both default to on. Changes apply immediately (read on the next round) with no need to regenerate the agents. When off, that agent no longer sees the constraints.

experimental.title: Experimental Features
experimental.desc:
These features are still under validation and default to off. They may change agent behavior or affect stability, so turn them on only after you understand the impact.

noa context compression: the model compresses long conversation history directly (norma v0.4.0). When on, the four kinds of agents connected to the platform (planner / worker / main agent / conversation) hand off context to noa instead of using the built-in compression, and the raw compression output is kept in the task's working directory for easy review. Changes apply immediately (to runs started afterward) with no need to regenerate the agents. Turning it off restores the built-in compression immediately.

webSearch.title: Web Search
webSearch.desc:
The master switch + source settings for web search. Only when it is on can you choose web_search usage individually in each agent's settings (it returns only the title/link/summary and does not fetch the body; body collection is handled by WebFetch). Web search does not go through the recording proxy and is independent of Traffic Capture.

For the source, you can choose among DuckDuckGo (ddgs) (no Key needed), Brave (free tier) (requires a Brave API Key), Tavily (requires a Tavily API Key), and DeepSeek (reuses the current LLM settings). When the master switch is off, each agent's web search switch is unavailable.
webSearch.on: Master switch on · Can be enabled individually in each agent's settings
webSearch.off: Off · Web search can't be enabled for any agent
webSearch.deepseekDesc1: This source reuses the currently active LLM settings as-is. So it supports only the official DeepSeek models, and those settings must use the anthropic protocol. DeepSeek's OpenAI-protocol endpoint does not support server-side search. Changing the LLM settings may stop this source from working.
webSearch.deepseekDesc2: Unlike other sources, the search is run by the DeepSeek server. Each search consumes one extra model call (incurring token cost), and the search request does not go through the egress proxy above and is not included in the traffic record. The returned results contain only titles and links (no summary); if you need the body, WebFetch fetches it.
webSearch.deepseekDesc3: You must verify yourself that the above conditions are met; the system does not block it. You can use the “Search Test” button below to actually run it once and check.
webSearch.braveNeedsKey: You selected Brave but haven't set a Key yet. The search tool won't turn on until you save a Key.

pool.title: LLM rotation · failover
pool.desc: When on, agents that don't specify a model automatically switch to the next profile whenever the current one is unusable (insufficient balance / expired key / rate limit / service error).

enable.label: Enable rotation
enable.hint: Off by default. When off, only the active profile is ever used, and a failure just fails.

bindFallback.label: Fall back even when a pinned model fails
bindFallback.hint: Off by default: when an agent or task pins a specific profile, only that profile is used and a failure just fails (no silent switch to another model). When on, a pinned profile that fails falls back to the rotation chain below.

order.label: Rotation order
order.tooFew: Only {n} profile(s) are currently usable, so rotation won't work. You need API Keys filled in and at least 2 profiles taking part in the rotation.

recoverNow.title: Recover now: clears the circuit breaker and retries this profile on the next call

pool.note: The active profile is always first; the rest follow in order of priority (set on each profile). When a profile fails it enters a cooldown (60s → 5min → 30min), is skipped during the cooldown, and is automatically brought back once it recovers. Profiles that can't fit the current request in their context window are skipped. Agents and tasks that pin a model don't take part in the rotation by default.

profile.descNew: A new profile isn't activated automatically. Use it by clicking "Set active" on its card.
profile.descEdit: Make your changes, then click Save. Saving the active profile applies it to all agents immediately.

model.label: Model
model.loadTitle: Load available models from the API

proxy.label: Proxy (optional)
proxy.hint: Only LLM outbound requests go through this proxy. Supports http/https/socks5 and may include a username and password (e.g. socks5://user:pass@host:port; URL-encode the password if it contains special characters). Leave empty to use no proxy (direct connection).

sessionHeader.label: Custom session header (optional)
sessionHeader.hint: Fill in a header name and this HTTP header is sent on every request, with its value automatically set to the current session's session id (conv-12 for chat sessions, exp3-worker-i87 for workers, etc.). It's for gateways that use a session-id header for prompt caching / sticky routing. The same session stays stable across turns, and different sessions differ from one another. Not sent if empty.

apiKey.placeholderSet: Set ({hint}); leave empty to keep it

profile.rateHint: Rate limit 0 = unlimited, shared by all agents. The context window is in K (thousands of tokens): 0 = default 200K, max 1000 (i.e. 1M). Set it too high and compaction won't be triggered.

priority.label: Rotation priority
priority.hint: Higher numbers are picked first. The active profile is always first regardless of this value. Profiles with the same priority take turns going first, naturally sharing the quota.

exclude.label: Exclude from rotation
exclude.hint: When on, this profile is never used as a failover target (it can still be used when an agent or task pins it explicitly). Good for an expensive profile you want "reserved for a specific agent, so it isn't consumed when others fail."

streaming.label: Streaming output · streaming
streaming.hint: When on (default), it runs over streaming SSE so you can watch real-time progress and live token counts during a run. When off, it runs truly non-streaming (stream:false, returning the full response at once), which can work around broken SSE implementations on some gateways (empty frames / frames missing the thinking field) but loses real-time progress during a run.

maxTokens.label: Output cap · max tokens
maxTokens.hint: The maximum number of tokens to generate in a single response, sent with every request. 0 (default) = don't send this field and follow the server default. This differs from the "Context window" above, which is the model's total capacity and is used only to compute the compaction threshold locally. Set it too small and a reasoning model gets cut off during the thinking stage and can't answer a single character.

maxTokensFieldHint.openai: Which key to send the cap under. max_tokens is the default and most compatible gateways recognize only this. OpenAI's official reasoning models (the o-series / GPT-5), on the other hand, recognize only max_completion_tokens and throw an unsupported_parameter error the moment they receive max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.anthropic: Selectable only in the openai format. Anthropic's field name is fixed to max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.openai-responses: Selectable only in the openai format. The Responses API's field name is fixed to max_output_tokens.

thinkingType.label: Thinking switch · thinking.type
thinkingType.hint: Controls whether the thinking field is sent. Don't send = omit this field (compatible with models that don't support it, such as MiniMax); Off = send disabled; On = send enabled. Independent of the effort below.

effort.label: Reasoning effort · reasoning_effort
effort.hint: An independent effort level (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Anthropic output_config.effort). Some interfaces have no thinking field and turn on reasoning through effort alone, so you can set effort on its own without sending the thinking switch.

toast.nameModelRequired: Enter a name and a model
toast.created: Created: {name} (use it by clicking "Set active" on its card)
toast.savedActive: Saved. The active profile applies immediately, no restart needed

connect.title: Connection retry
connect.trigger: When no connection is made or a 200 hasn't been received yet: network-layer errors such as connection reset / read-write timeout / DNS failure, plus HTTP 408·429·500·502·503·504.
connect.skips: Other status codes (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422, etc.) are definitive rejections that would fail the same way on a resend, so they're passed straight up.
connect.desc: Resends the same request as-is. Once a stream has started (a 200 was already received), this layer no longer handles a mid-stream drop.
connect.offHint: -1 = never retry; pass the failure straight up

empty.title: Empty-response retry
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 with a normal finish_reason of stop, but the entire response contains no content block. Gateway empty frames, frames missing the thinking field, and sampling hiccups all show up this way.
empty.skips: Excludes cases where content is empty because it was cut off by max_tokens (that must be solved by raising the output cap; a resend just hits the same wall again).
empty.desc: It resends the entire prompt, which is costly on long contexts, so it's best not to set the count high.

stream.title: Same-provider safe-window retry
stream.where: This project · before any output is delivered
stream.trigger: A problem that arises after the stream is already established (a 200 was received): a mid-stream disconnect, provider overloaded, or a 429 / 5xx error event inside the stream, while not a single token has yet been delivered to the caller.
stream.skips: Doesn't retry quota exhaustion (402 / insufficient_quota, handled by rotation switching profiles), context overflow (413 / context length, handled by compaction), or the definitive rejections 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422.
stream.desc: Replays the same request on the same profile. Since no output has been delivered yet, replaying doesn't duplicate model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = on a stream drop, hand off immediately to the outer intent re-run layer

breaker.title: Rotation circuit breaker
breaker.where: This project · per process, one global instance
breaker.trigger: Trips when transient failures (429 · 5xx · network errors) pile up consecutively to the threshold. Definitive failures such as insufficient balance (402), expired key (401 / 403), and missing model (404) trip immediately from the first one, ignoring the threshold.
breaker.skips: A single success resets the count to 0, so a profile that only acts up occasionally won't gradually accumulate its way to tripping.
breaker.desc: When tripped, it enters a cooldown, and during the cooldown rotation skips this profile. The state is stored in the DB, so it survives a restart.
breaker.offHint: -1 = never trip on transient failures (definitive failures still trip)

intent.title: Intent re-run
intent.where: This project · per process, one global instance
intent.trigger: When the earlier layers couldn't stop it: a worker ends in model_error. Either the inner retries are all exhausted, or the stream dropped after it had already begun delivering output (replay isn't safe then, so the whole thing has to be run again).
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is already handled by rotation switching profiles, so it isn't re-run here. When a task enters pause / stop / wrap-up, it yields immediately and doesn't take up backoff time.
intent.desc: Runs the entire intent again from the start. As the outermost layer, a single re-run multiplies the counts of all the inner layers once more.
intent.offHint: -1 = don't re-run; mark the intent as blocked right away

retry.emptyLine: Leave empty to use the default. {hint}.

override.label: Retry override
override.hint: Applies to this profile only, overriding the global defaults in "Retry & backoff." Leave a field empty to follow the global value. Enter -1 for the count to turn off this layer's retries. Fill in an interval to use a fixed interval instead of exponential backoff. The circuit breaker and intent re-run are per process, so they can be adjusted only on the global page.

retry.intro: A single model-call failure passes through five retry layers in order from innermost to outermost: <chain>connection → empty response → same-provider safe window → rotation circuit breaker → intent re-run</chain>. An outer layer's turn comes only after the inner one is used up, so the counts <emph>multiply together</emph>. Max out every layer and a single hiccup can burn dozens of requests. Leaving them all empty is the current default, exactly the behavior when this page didn't exist. The first three layers can be overridden individually on each model profile.

toast.saved: Saved. Applies immediately (a call already in progress keeps using the previous values)

notifyPage.title: Notifications
notifyPage.subtitle: When a vulnerability is found, send notifications to channels like DingTalk, Feishu, and WeCom. Each channel can have its own delivery timing and filter rules.

toast.testSent: Test message sent ({ms} ms). Please check the channel

global.title: Global settings
global.baseUrlHint: The address the message's "View details" button points to. Leave blank to omit the button.
global.digestHint: Applies only to channels in "Digest" mode.

sheet.kindLocked: Channel type cannot be changed. Changing the type is equivalent to replacing all credentials, so please create a new channel.
sheet.noFields: The input form for this channel is not defined yet (no CHANNEL_FIELDS entry in the frontend). Add the entry and try again.
sheet.modeDigest: Digest · one bundled message per interval
sheet.modeHint: For something like "high and above in real-time, the rest as a digest," create two channels. Set one to real-time + minimum severity High, and the other to digest + no severity limit.
sheet.rateHint: Leave blank to use the channel default. 0 means unlimited. When the limit is exceeded, messages are delayed rather than dropped.

filter.title: Filter rules (leave blank for no filtering)
filter.includeHint: One keyword per line. Case-insensitive substring matching. Blank means all types.
filter.excludeHint: Exclusion takes priority over inclusion. If both match, the item is excluded.
filter.idsHint: Leave task/asset blank for no limit. If set, the vulnerability must intersect with them.
filter.onStatusChange: Also send when a vulnerability's handling status changes (real-time mode only)

secret.label: Signing secret
secret.help: Enter this when you select "Signature" in the bot's security settings. Leave blank if you chose "Custom keywords" or did not enable security settings.

secret.label: Signature verification secret
secret.help: Enter this when "Signature verification" is enabled on the bot; otherwise leave it blank.

headers.label: Custom request headers
headers.help: One KEY=VALUE per line. Example: Authorization=Bearer xxx

body_template.label: Request body template
body_template.help: Leave blank to use the built-in default template. Variables: '{{.Title}} {{.Batch}} {{.Count}} {{.HomeURL}} {{.SentAt}}', plus .Name/.VulnClass/.Severity/.Summary/.Assets/.DetailURL/.StatusLabel under range .Items. When inserting a string, use '{{json .Xxx}}' instead of '{{.Xxx}}'; otherwise quotes in the title will break the JSON.

base_url.label: API URL
base_url.help: Leave blank to use the official URL. Enter this when using your own Bot API reverse proxy.

port.label: Port
port.help: Port 587 uses STARTTLS. For 465, enable "Implicit TLS."

tls.label: Implicit TLS
tls.help: Enable for port 465 and disable for port 587 (STARTTLS is used automatically).
